summary: Lists the numbers assigned for networks, protocols and similar identifiers used in the early Internet. Such lists were reissued as assignments changed. This RFC is historic. Replaced by RFC 776.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 770 collects assigned numbers used by network protocols, with tables for networks, protocol fields, ports or sockets, and links. It was intended to be updated periodically and was later replaced by RFC 776.

subtitle: A 1980 edition of the assigned-number lists for network protocols

tldr.problem: Network protocol implementations use assigned values, and developers need to know which values have been assigned.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC gathers several registries, including network, IP version, protocol, port or socket, and link numbers.
tldr.outcome: RFC 770 is Historic and was later replaced by RFC 776.

today: RFC 770 is Historic and has been obsoleted by RFC 776.

sections.title: Purpose of the Registry
sections.content:
RFC 770 records values assigned from several number series used in network protocol implementations. It says the list will be updated periodically and that current information and new assignments can be obtained from Jon Postel.

The RFC directs developers who need a link, socket or similar value to request an assignment. It points readers to the RFC series and the Protocol Handbook for protocol details.
sections.plainLanguage: This document gathers number assignments used by several protocols. Developers who need a new number are asked to request an assignment.

sections.title: Network and Protocol Fields
sections.content:
The registry lists network numbers, Internet Protocol versions, protocol numbers, and message types and formats. The network number field is 8 bits; the IP version field is 4 bits; and the IP Protocol field is 8 bits and identifies the next-level protocol.

For example, the protocol-number table lists User Datagram at 17. Other entries include assigned values, reserved values and ranges left unassigned in this edition.
sections.plainLanguage: Separate tables identify networks and protocol details with numbers. The tables also show which values are reserved or have not yet been assigned.

sections.title: Ports, Sockets and Links
sections.content:
The RFC lists port numbers for TCP and socket numbers for the ARPANET Host-to-Host protocol. It explains that a server uses a contact socket or port so callers can reach a service. The same section lists link numbers used in the Host/IMP interface.

RFC 770 is Historic. The unit metadata records RFC 776 as its replacement.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry also lists numbers used to contact services and identify links. A later assigned-numbers edition, RFC 776, replaced this one.
